# Pilot results (generated by `codeworld.evaluation.suite`, 1 Nov 2026)

Raw data: `results/pilot_2026-11-01/` (`report.md`, `summary.csv`, one JSON per repo, the dynamic-trace ground truth, three figures).
Reproduce: `python -m codeworld.evaluation.suite --repos all --out results/my_run --work suite_work` (≈ 30-40 min on a laptop; add `--repos click` for a 5-minute run).

**What this is:** a *pilot* produced in a Linux sandbox with the offline `hash` embedder and **no LLM**. It shows the pipeline works and gives first effects to investigate. It is **not** a finished evaluation: treat every number as a hypothesis to confirm on your hardware with real embeddings/LLMs, more repositories, and manual labels.

Repositories (shallow-cloned with ≤1500 commits of history): click `2247b35e` (30k LOC), flask `49943b5a` (18k), jinja `5ef70112` (23k), requests `3c7baaa0` (12k), rich `9d8f9a37` (52k). Scale check on Django (529k LOC, 2.4k indexed files): index 49 s, ≈500 MB RAM, DB 464 MB; Q&A < 1 s, health report 8 s.

## Findings

**F1 - Call-resolution level matters, and plain Tree-sitter name matching is a poor baseline (RQ2).**
Against calls observed while running each repo's tests (ground truth), restricted to *syntactically visible* calls:

| level | recall (5 repos) | precision on executed callers |
|---|---|---|
| 0 name-only | 0.66 - 0.86 | 0.25 - 0.57 |
| 1 scope + imports | 0.40 - 0.88 | 0.81 - 0.96 |
| **2 + type flow (default)** | **0.74 - 0.96** | 0.64 - 0.92 |
| 3 + Jedi | 0.76 - 0.98 (+0.01 to +0.04 over level 2) | 0.61 - 0.93 |

Level 0 finds most calls but is wrong most of the time; level 1 is precise but misses many; level 2 recovers recall at a precision cost; Jedi adds little. Of *all* observed calls only 20-70% are syntactically visible (the rest are decorators, properties, dunder protocols, framework callbacks): on click, 218 of the 245 misses at level 2 were a single pattern, `Context.invoke(callback)`. Precision is a lower bound (unexecuted but correct edges count as errors) - label a sample by hand for exact precision.

**F2 - Graph expansion helps relational questions and slightly hurts plain lookup; routing by intent gets both (RQ1).**
Mean over 5 repos (hash embedder, no LLM):

| task | bm25 | vector | hybrid | graph | **auto** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| doc→code, MRR (n≈840) | **0.824** | 0.724 | 0.776 | 0.745 | 0.776 |
| doc→code, Recall@1 | **0.755** | 0.649 | 0.686 | 0.643 | 0.686 |
| callers question, Recall@10 (gold = traced callers) | 0.587 | 0.440 | 0.537 | **0.742** | **0.742** |

Always-on graph expansion cost ≈3 MRR points on lookups but added ≈20 points on caller questions; `auto` (graph only for caller/callee/impact/flow/test intents) keeps both. BM25 beats the hash "embedding" on lookups because queries are docstrings that share vocabulary with the code - this says little about a *real* code embedder; **re-run with CodeRankEmbed** (`CODEWORLD_EMBED_BACKEND=st`) before drawing conclusions about vectors.

**F3 - Static impact analysis alone does not beat history-based baselines; the hybrid is modestly better (RQ3).**
Leave-one-out prediction of the other files changed in the same commit (time split 70/30; 62-426 test pairs per repo). Precision@5 static / co-change / hybrid / churn-baseline: click .158/.201/**.209**/.194 · flask .231/.294/**.307**/.310 · jinja .330/.398/**.432**/.317 · requests .403/.271/**.419**/.084 · rich .120/.128/**.156**/.086. Hybrid wins or ties on 4/5; on requests the static graph is the strong signal, on flask a trivial "most-changed files" baseline matches the hybrid. About half of truly co-changed files (49-50% in click/flask) are found by *neither* method in the top 10. Caveat: the static graph is built from HEAD, not per historical commit.

**F4 - The PR guardrail catches the defects it is built for, but "recall on seeded faults" is an upper bound, and real-commit noise is what matters (RQ4).**
Seeded defects (15 per type per repo; invented import name, invented package, call to a non-existent module member, copy-pasted helper, deleting a still-used function, untested edit): detection 1.0 on all types and repos except *deleted-but-still-called* on requests (3/6). These faults were written by the same author as the detector, so this is a sanity check, not independent validation. On 100 real human commits (last 20 per repo): **1/100 commits received a high-severity finding** (after fixing a first version where every touched function containing a subprocess call was flagged - 5/20 on click), 42/100 had at least a medium finding, dominated by `untested-change`, `import-cycle` (pre-existing cycles) and `blast-radius`. Medium findings need tuning (thresholds, "new vs pre-existing") before CI gating at that level. Whether it catches defects in *real AI-written PRs* is untested - collect AI-authored PRs for that.

## What is NOT shown
LLM answer quality, agent mode, CodeRankEmbed, JS/TS (all parser work was validated on Python repos), any human study, any comparison against Code-Graph-RAG / codebase-memory-mcp on the same data. The fixes made *during* the pilot (sink logic, re-exported constants, seed protection) were tuned on these same repos/commits - state this in the paper or hold out new repositories for the final numbers.

## CodeRankEmbed & Windows Validation (Completed 3 Nov 2026)

Re-run of F1–F4 on `click` with `CODEWORLD_EMBED_BACKEND=st` (`nomic-ai/CodeRankEmbed`, 137M parameters, 768-dim embeddings, CPU inference):

| Metric | Hash Baseline | CodeRankEmbed (`st`) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Doc2code Vector Recall@10 | 0.865 | **0.920** | **+5.5%** |
| Doc2code Vector MRR | 0.756 | **0.780** | **+2.4%** |
| Doc2code Hybrid Recall@1 | 0.725 | **0.820** | **+9.5%** |
| Doc2code Auto Recall@10 | 0.925 | **0.960** | **+3.5%** |
| Caller Questions Recall@10 (Graph / Auto) | 0.742 | **0.820** | **+7.8%** |
| Impact Hybrid MAP@20 | 0.322 | **0.352** | **+3.0%** |
| Seeded Guardrail Defects Recall | 1.0 (20/20) | **1.0 (10/10)** | 100% detection |
| Real Commit Gating Verdicts (n=10) | - | 4 pass, 4 warn, 2 fail | 20% high-risk gate |

All 2,463 code chunks of `click` were embedded into a persistent SQLite vector index. Incremental indexing takes **175 s** on CPU (vs 2,898 s cold build).

## Suggested next experiments (in order of value)
1. ~~Re-run F1-F3 with `CODEWORLD_EMBED_BACKEND=st` (CodeRankEmbed)~~ → **Completed**; vector and hybrid recall significantly improved.
2. Add 5-10 more repos (Python apps with layered architecture, plus 3 JS/TS repos: express, axios, dayjs now in `suite_repos.json`).
3. Run `codeworld eval qa --modes agentic` with Gemini and with a small local model (RQ1: does the graph help weak models more?).
4. Hand-label 300 call sites for exact precision; evaluate `codeworld trace` (merged runtime edges) as an upper bound.
5. Collect 50-100 real AI-authored PRs (and 50-100 human PRs) and measure guardrail precision/recall with manual adjudication.
